questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates advanced telemetry architecture, per-tenant observability, dynamic sampling strategies, and operational safety practices for CNF gateways at scale.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry, OTLP, trace context propagation, and baggage
- Namespace-scoped configuration and feature flags
- Adaptive sampling policies with latency-aware thresholds
- Canary rollouts and rollback safety

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.trace
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.trace.enabled: "true"
  cnf.trace.sample-rate: "0.25"
  cnf.trace.target: "otel-collector.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:4317"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf-gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.trace
              key: cnf.trace.target
      - name: otel-collector
        image: otel/collector:latest
        args: ["--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: otel-config
          mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:
      - name: otel-config
        configMap:
          name: otel-collector-config
```

## Adaptive Sampling Implementation
```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {
    baseRate := sampleRate
    if errorRate > 0.05 {
        return min(1.0, baseRate*2)
    }
    return baseRate
}
```

## Rollout Strategy
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: error-rate-check
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        failedRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the candidate's ability to design cross-service tracing with per-tenant opt-in, stable sampling, and practical OpenTelemetry integration in a CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway environment.

## Key Concepts

- **Tenant-scoped opt-in** via namespace annotations and ConfigMaps
- **Stable sampling decisions** using deterministic hashing (tenantID + path)
- **OpenTelemetry Collector** configuration with OTLP receiver and Jaeger exporter
- **Per-namespace ConfigMaps** for feature flags and sampling rates
- **Trace context propagation** across microservices using W3C TraceContext

## Expected Answer Components

1. **Per-tenant sidecar/init container** that reads namespace annotations and ConfigMap values
2. **OpenTelemetry SDK configuration** with deterministic sampling logic
3. **Collector pipeline** with OTLP intake and Jaeger export
4. **Test manifest** demonstrating single-namespace deployment
5. **Validation steps** for verifying traces appear correctly in Jaeger

## Red Flags in Answers

- No mention of tenant isolation or annotation-based opt-in
- Random sampling without consistency across services
- Missing trace context propagation
- No Jaeger integration or export configuration
- Hardcoded sampling rates without per-tenant configuration

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a per-tenant provenance flow, integrate image signing and SBOMs, and apply admission controls with policy-as-code. It also checks practical knowledge of Gatekeeper/OPA integration, namespace-scoped policies, and minimal test workflows.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing with tenant-specific keys
- SPDX SBOM attachment and verification
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Per-tenant policy in a ConfigMap
- Minimal manifests and kubectl validation in a single namespace

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers
        not startswith(c.image, "ghcr.io/")
        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance
metadata:
  name: per-tenant-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
# Compliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway-bad
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: unsigned/gateway:latest
```

```bash
# Kubectl steps (one namespace first)
kubectl create ns tenant-a
# 1) Register constraint template and constraint
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_template.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_constraint.yaml
# 2) Sign and SBOM-attach a valid image (tenant-a key)
cosign sign --key cosign-tenant-a.key ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
# 3) Deploy compliant manifest
kubectl apply -f compliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 4) Deploy noncompliant manifest (unsigned)
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 5) Check Gatekeeper denials and logs
kubectl get events -n tenant-a
kubectl describe deployment tenant-a-gateway-bad -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you extend to multi-tenant namespaces concurrently?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical per-tenant traffic routing, feature flag management, and end-to-end validation with minimal manifests in CNF/Kubernetes environments.

## Key Concepts
- Sidecar-based traffic routing with per-tenant control
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMap for cnf.canary.enabled and cnf.canary.sample-rate
- Deterministic hashing for consistent bucket allocation
- Minimal YAML manifests for quick validation

## Code Example

**Namespace-scoped ConfigMap:**
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.canary
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.canary.enabled: "true"
  cnf.canary.sample-rate: "5"
```

**Canary Deployment:**
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: canary-resource
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  selector:
    app: resource
    version: canary
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: stable-resource
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  selector:
    app: resource
    version: stable
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
```

**Sidecar Configuration:**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: cnf-gateway:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: cnf-config
              mountPath: /config
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: cnf-config
          configMap:
            name: cnf.canary
```

## Validation
Apply the manifests and verify routing:
```bash
kubectl apply -f namespace.yaml
kubectl apply -f configmap.yaml
kubectl apply -f services.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

# Test canary routing
export TENANT_ID="tenant-a"
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -H "X-TENANT-ID: $TENANT_ID" http://cnf-gateway.tenant-a.svc/v2/resource
done
```

Expected: ~5% of requests route to canary-resource, 95% to stable-resource based on deterministic tenant ID hashing.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of policy-as-code, admission controls, and CNF feature gating in a real multi-tenant cluster.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped CRD for featurePolicy
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with Rego logic
- Per-tenant policy propagation in CI
- In-namespace tests for allow/deny scenarios

## Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: featurepolicies.example.com
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featurepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenant:
                type: string
              allowedFlags:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
```
```rego
package gatekeeper.featurepolicy

violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
  annotations := input.review.object.metadata.annotations
  feature := annotations["cnf/feature"]
  policy := data.tenants[input.review.object.metadata.namespace]
  not featureR in policy.allowedFlags
  msg := sprintf("disallowed feature flag: %v for tenant: %v", [feature, input.review.object.metadata.namespace])
}
```
